subject: Pharmacology
concept: Antithrombotic medicines reduce coagulation or promote fibrin breakdown.

content.definition: Antithrombotic medicines reduce coagulation or promote fibrin breakdown.
content.explanation: Heparins act through antithrombin; warfarin reduces vitamin-K-dependent clotting factor synthesis; direct oral anticoagulants inhibit thrombin or factor Xa; fibrinolytics promote plasmin-mediated fibrin breakdown.
content.mechanism: Heparins act through antithrombin; warfarin reduces vitamin-K-dependent clotting factor synthesis; direct oral anticoagulants inhibit thrombin or factor Xa; fibrinolytics promote plasmin-mediated fibrin breakdown.
content.clinical_relevance: Anticoagulants mainly prevent clot propagation, whereas fibrinolytics actively dissolve established fibrin thrombi.
high_yield: Anticoagulants mainly prevent clot propagation, whereas fibrinolytics actively dissolve established fibrin thrombi.
content.treatment: Therapy is indication- and patient-specific and should follow current authoritative guidance rather than a fixed universal regimen.
effects: Bleeding is the principal adverse effect; anticoagulant choice depends on indication, renal function, interactions and bleeding risk.

yemen_context.relevance: Relevant to the Hematology block and infectious-disease pharmacology; local availability and national guidance may differ.
yemen_context.evidence: General evidence; no Yemen-specific regimen asserted.

review_notes: Original educational synthesis; treatment is intentionally presented as principles rather than patient-specific prescribing.
